This Widebody Chevy Camaro Has a Biblical Mod, What’s Your Take on the Message?
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | rohanawheels
Even though we are perfectly capable of writing a story about the Chevrolet Camaro without reminding ourselves that this model is dead and buried, we refuse to do that. Well, at least until General Motors brings back this iconic nameplate.
That might happen in late 2028, probably for the 2029 model year, as the moniker is indeed coming back from the dead. However, instead of launching it as a two-door coupe, perhaps joined by a two-door convertible body style, it appears that the bowtie brand has settled for something else instead: a four-door sedan.
Word on the street is that the next-generation Chevrolet Camaro might only be offered as a sedan, so it will inevitably take on the four-door version of the modern-day Dodge Charger. For what it’s worth, it will likely annihilate it, at least from an enthusiast’s perspective, because it will launch with V8 firepower, and probably a stick shift channeling the yet-unknown output and thrust to the rear wheels.
But the new-age Dodge Charger is also getting a V8 engine for the first time ever, so it will finally be able to take a proper swing at the S650 Ford Mustang. The latter is the only muscle car in production to be offered with a V8. And given that the new Chevy Camaro will launch as a four-door, and that the latest Charger is also offered in this body style, it is possible that the Dearborn company might eventually consider launching a Mustang Sedan.
Photo: Instagram | rohanawheels Now, that’s a story for another time (actually, it’s been discussed many times), so instead, we should get back on track and start writing about the pictured Chevrolet Camaro , which looks extremely muscular due to its aftermarket makeover. The first thing that stands out is the widebody design, highlighted by the wider wheel arches at the front and the extremely broad shoulders, joined by a new hood that is also on the muscular side of things.
Moreover, there is also a new apron attached to the front bumper, and by the looks of it, it is adjustable. The side skirt attachments are also new, and at the rear, it seems to sport new taillights. The rear bumper is new, and so is the diffuser, and this component is on the very large side of things. Not only that, but it also features cutouts in the middle for the four exhaust tips. The trunk lid is decorated with a large wing, and there are also attachments on the rear windscreen, and the rear three-quarter windows.
Rohana shared pictures of this modded Chevrolet Camaro on its social media channels earlier this week for a very simple reason: it rides on one of their wheel sets. The alloys are called the Rohana Forged RFG29. This model is available in unibloc and trinity options, with hidden, fully exposed, or 50/50 hardware, and can be specified with carbon fiber options, and ordered in several premium and custom finishes.
Photo: Instagram | rohanawheels The sizes available range from 18 to 24 inches, and the widths from 8.5 to 13 inches, respectively, and the starting price of the full set in the smallest offering available is $6,000. That’s before factoring in other options, and before buying the tires, obviously. In this case, the Y-spoke wheels feature a black look, have the Rohana logo on the 3D center caps, and they spin around the red brake calipers that sport Brembo branding in white on them.
The brake calipers are the things that provide the most contrast to this Chevy Camaro’s exterior, as the muscle car in question is presented in black. Now, about that Biblical reference made in the title, it is all about the new trim on the front fenders. These read “Psalm 23:4,” and that says “Even though I walk through the darkest valley (the valley of the shadow of death), I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.” And that’s definitely a very strong message.
The interior of this muscle car, which also features a Rohana decal on the front windscreen, is only partially visible through the windows in the images shared online by the wheelmaker recently. Still, we can see that the seats are shown in red, and that’s likely leather upholstery, and the pillars and headliner are black. We reckon a bit more red could also be on deck on the inside, but that’s our two cents, and should be taken accordingly.
Now, this is a very impressive-looking Chevrolet Camaro that definitely deserves its 15 minutes of online fame, hence why decided to share it with you. But I promise we can still be friends even if you do not dig the way this tuned muscle car looks. So, what’s your take on it? Is the tuning job a yay or a nay in your book?
